title: Space weather in real time: the solar wind and interplanetary field at L1, the planetary K index, the Sun's X-rays and energetic protons from GOES
provider: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC), from DSCOVR, ACE and IMAP's real-time solar wind, ground magnetometers, and the GOES satellites

now.description: The feeds as they are at the retrieval

feeds.about: the solar wind's protons at L1, one-minute values of the last day, newest first; rows flagged active are from the spacecraft in use (proton_speed km/s, proton_density cm⁻³, proton_temperature K; time_tag UTC)
the interplanetary magnetic field at L1, one-minute values, newest first (bt, bx, by, bz in nT, in GSE and GSM axes)
the estimated planetary K index, three-hourly, of the last week, oldest first
the primary GOES satellite's X-ray flux in 0.05–0.4 nm and 0.1–0.8 nm (W/m²), one-minute values of six hours, oldest first
the primary GOES satellite's integral proton fluxes above 1, 5, 10, 30, 50, 60, 100 and 500 MeV (pfu = cm⁻² s⁻¹ sr⁻¹), five-minute values, oldest first

format: JSON arrays of records with a UTC time tag. Read live by applications' servers (applications/cosmopoiesis-lab/runtime.py) at the feeds' cadences; a retrieval through the fetcher keeps a snapshot.
coverage: The present: the last six hours to the last week, depending on the feed; the real-time solar wind is preliminary, not the science-quality record
licence: US Government work, public domain (NOAA SWPC's data are freely available; SWPC asks that it be credited)
citation: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center, https://www.swpc.noaa.gov/
